notes: Only the materialized Agreement is written; RL2 states that the Offer is inert for Eval, and due2 has no Offer-to-Agreement transformation. rl2:prerequisiteDuty on both read Privileges becomes odrl:duty on both permissions, pointing at one named duty, so one attestation serves both (ODRL IM §2.6.5). The attestation is not a clause of the RL2 Agreement, so it is not an obligation here either. It names the Provider as assignee; without it, role inheritance would make the Consumer the bearer and the Provider's attestation would not be a witness. The Promises become root obligations, in force whenever a permission of the Agreement matches the request (§5.2). ex:historyPortDuty is direct: no evidence of ex:deliverInitialLoad means outstanding, RL2's Pending for an unbounded Achievement Duty. ex:dailyPortDuty's Maintain invariant has no due2 form; the closest is a remedial obligation (refresh the port) guarded by portAge > PT18H, so RL2's Active maps to 'not in force' and Violated to 'in force, outstanding'. The standing divergence on unfulfilled preconditions applies to scenarios 2 and 3. Scenarios 2 and 3 are added.

expected.why: ex:readDailyPortPrivilege_A1 applies; ex:ev1 is a witness for ex:attestConformance_A1 (actor ex:Provider, action, object, before effective_at), so the candidate is ready. The permission matches, so the obligations are in force subject to their guards: ex:historyPortDuty has none and no witness (outstanding, RL2 Pending); ex:dailyPortDuty's guard PT4H > PT18H is F, so it is not in force (RL2 Active).

scenarios.name: read daily port, no attestation yet

expected.why: ex:readDailyPortPrivilege_A1 applies; its duty has no witness, so it is outstanding and the candidate is pending (no deadline, never violated). ex:historyPortDuty is in force and outstanding; ex:dailyPortDuty's guard is F.

scenarios.name: read history port, attestation by the wrong party, daily port stale

expected.why: ex:readHistoryPortPrivilege_A1 applies. ex:ev2's actor is ex:Consumer, not the duty's assignee ex:Provider, so it is no witness; the shared duty is outstanding and the candidate pending. The history-port permission matching suffices to put the policy's obligations in force: ex:dailyPortDuty's guard PT20H > PT18H holds and it has no witness (RL2 would call the Maintain duty Violated), and ex:historyPortDuty is outstanding.
